newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian small business sees static economy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian small business sees static economy.

text.p: Most Australian small businesses believe the economy is either standing still or in recession, but the minority of businesses expecting a pick-up has risen, according to a survey released on Wednesday.

The survey, conducted by Telstra Corp's half-owned telephone directory subsidiary Yellow Pages Australia, showed 62 percent of small business operators believe the economy has stalled and 18 percent believe it is in recession.

The random survey of 1,200 small businesses across Australia was conducted from October 23 to November 6 and covered their experience over the October quarter and their expectations for the 12 months ending November 1997, Yellow Pages said.
The proportion of small businesses expecting an economic pick-up over the next 12 months rose to 35 percent from 25 percent in the August survey, it said.
The latest survey just coincided with the Reserve Bank's move on November 6 to cut the official cash interest rate by 50 basis points to 6.5 percent. The followed a similar easing in late July.

"The previous half-a-percent rate cut (on July 31) did nothing to lift the performance or confidence of the small business sector. One would hope that the latest cut will have a real impact," said Yellow Page's economic adviser, John Marsden, in a statement.
